title: Use MCP tools
content_data:
Use this endpoint to send MCP requests to the server path using a bearer access token, ensuring the token you present is valid for this specific MCP server path. # Request **Endpoint** https://business-api.tiktok.com/open_mcp/{server}/ **Method** POST **Header** ```xtable |Field{28%}|Data Type{18%}|Description{54%}| |---|---|---| | Authorization {Required} | string | The access token in the format of `Bearer {{Access-Token}}`.
The access token must be valid for the specific MCP `server` path. | ``` **Path parameters** ```xtable |Field{28%}|Data Type{18%}|Description{54%}| |---|---|---| |server {Required}|string|The specific TikTok for Business MCP server URL.

Enum values: `tt-ads-mcp-flat`, `tt-ads-mcp-layer`.

To learn more about how these server URLs differ, see [Choose your server URL](https://business-api.tiktok.com/portal/docs/how-to-connect-a-custom-agent-to-tiktok-for-business-mcp-server/v1.3#anchor-3).| ``` **Body parameters** ```xtable |Field{28%}|Data Type{18%}|Description{54%}| |---|---|---| |jsonrpc {Required}|string|The version of the JSON-RPC protocol you are using.

Enum value: `2.0`.| |id {Required}|integer|A unique identifier you assign to the request.

You will receive this same ID in the response so you can match them.| |method {Required}|string|The specific MCP method you want to use.

Enum values:
  • `tools/list`: To retrieve available tools.
  • `tools/call`: To execute a specific tool.
| |params {Required}|object|The parameter payload you supply for the method.
  • When `method` is `tools/list`, provide an empty object (`{}`) .
  • When `method` is `tools/call`, provide specific tool arguments.
| ``` ## Example > **Note**
> The example below uses `tt-ads-mcp-layer` as the `{server}` value. You can replace this with your chosen server value. ### Retrieve available tools ```xcodeblock (code curl http) curl --location --request POST 'https://business-api.tiktok.com/open_mcp/tt-ads-mcp-layer' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer {{Access-Token}}' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data '{ "jsonrpc": "2.0",1 "id": {{id}}, "method": "tools/list", "params": {} }' (/code) ``` ### Execute a specific tool ```xcodeblock (code curl http) curl --location --request POST 'https://business-api.tiktok.com/open_mcp/tt-ads-mcp-layer' \ --header 'Access-Token: {{Access-Token}}' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data '{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": {{id}}, "method": "tools/call", "params": { "name": "advertiser_info_get", "arguments": { "advertiser_ids": [ "{{advertiser_ids}}" ], "fields": [ "name", "status", "currency", "timezone" ] } } }' (/code) ``` # Response ```xtable |Field{28%}|Data Type{18%}|Description{54%}| |---|---|---| | jsonrpc | string | The version of the JSON-RPC protocol.

Enum value: `2.0`. | | id | integer | The identifier you originally sent, which you use to map this response to the correct request. | | result | object | The outcome of your request. You will find the list of tools or the tool execution output here. | #|tools | object[] | Returned only when `method` is set to `tools/list` in the request.

The list of tools you can access on this server.

You can inspect the `name`, `description`, and `inputSchema` of each tool to construct future execution calls. | #|content | object[] | Returned only when `method` is set to `tools/call` in the request.

The output generated by the tool you called.

You will extract the tool's specific output data from this array. | ``` ## Example ### Retrieve available tools ```xcodeblock (code curl http) { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": {{id}}, "result": { "tools": [ { "annotations": { "readOnlyHint": true }, "description": "{{description}}", "inputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "advertiser_ids": { "description": "{{description}}", "items": { "type": "string" }, "type": "array" }, "fields": { "description": "{{description}}", "items": { "enum": [ "telephone_number", "contacter", "currency", "cellphone_number", "timezone", "advertiser_id", "role", "company", "status", "description", "rejection_reason", "address", "name", "language", "industry", "license_no", "email", "license_url", "country", "balance", "create_time", "display_timezone", "owner_bc_id", "company_name_editable", "can_use_custom_identity", "ads_only_mode" ], "type": "string" }, "type": "array" } }, "required": [ "advertiser_ids" ] }, "name": "advertiser_info_get" }, { "annotations": { "readOnlyHint": true }, "description": "{{description}}", "inputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "advertiser_id": { "description": "{{description}}", "type": "string" }, "app_id": { "description": "{{description}}", "type": "string" } }, "required": [ "advertiser_id", "app_id" ] }, "name": "app_info_get" }, ... ] } } (/code) ``` ### Execute a specific tool ```xcodeblock (code curl http) { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": {{id}}, "result": { "content": [ { "type": "text", "text": "{\"data\":{\"list\":[{\"name\":\"{{name}}\",\"currency\":\"USD\",\"timezone\":\"Etc/GMT-8\",\"status\":\"STATUS_ENABLE\"}]},\"code\":0,\"message\":\"OK\",\"request_id\":\"{{request_id}}\"}" } ] } } (/code) ``` ## Error response When accessing MCP tools, authentication errors follow standard OAuth 2.0 Bearer Token semantics (RFC 6750). The server will return a `WWW-Authenticate` header containing the exact reason for the failure. ```xtable |HTTP Status Code{20%}|Meaning{30%}|Note{50%}| |---|---|---| |`401`|Missing token|A `WWW-Authenticate` challenge is returned.| |`401`|Invalid, expired, or revoked token|`WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token"` is returned.| |`403`|Insufficient scope|`WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope"` may be returned.| ```
